records.quote: Counterexample 3.1 For σ = 0.5 and i = 1, 2, 3, let Ti ∼ LL (σ, λi ) and Wi ∼ LL (σ, βi ) be two sets of mutually independent random variables. Let (v1 , v2 , v3 ) = (0.4, 0.4, 0.1) and (v1∗ , v2∗ , v3∗ ) = (0.5, 0.4, 0.2), where vi = 1/(1+λi^σ) and vi∗ = 1/(1+βi^σ). Now if h(p)= (2, 2, 1) and h(p∗ )= (3, 2, 1) are taken, where h(u) = − log(u), then it can be written that [h(p); v] >w [h(p∗ ); v∗], where (v, h(p)) ∈ Un , and (v ∗ , h(p∗ )) ∈ Un . The figure given below also shows that, for all 0 ≤ x ≤ 1, FX3:3 (x) ≤ FY3:3 (x) giving that X3:3 ≥st Y3:3 .
records.family: log-Lindley LL(σ, λ), σ = 0.5 common; vi = 1/(1+λi^σ)
records.compared: matrix-majorized parameter pairs (v, h(p)) vs (v*, h(p*))

hypotheses.formal: [h(p); v] >w [h(p*); v*] matrix weak majorization, both in Un

conclusion.direction: X3:3 >=st Y3:3 (F_X3:3(x) <= F_Y3:3(x) for all 0 <= x <= 1; Y side smaller)
